title: Trading $20,000 with AI agents on Robinhood: what's working, what isn't
author: Unfair_Set_355
selftext:
Robinhood account: $20,399.51, up $211.58 (up 1.05%) today.



Whole book including the Kalshi and Coinbase sleeves: $21,014.34, up $288.56 (up 1.39%) today.



I started with $10,000 and added another $10,000 a couple of weeks ago once it was going well. Profit since the start, deposits taken out: up $323.63.



The strategies, and how they're doing:



The Kneeler (Kalshi, NFL). Late in games, once the leading team is running out the clock, it buys NO on stat lines that can't realistically be hit anymore. That's usually at 88 to 99 cents, and it collects the dollar at the final whistle. It's 89 for 89 across five game days. This Sunday was 11 for 11 and made $13.81. All time it's up $85 after fees on $644 put in.



FAANG+ Momentum ($5,155.79, up $112.36 today, best day in the book). Each morning it reranks the biggest tech names by short-term momentum and holds the leaders. Today it sold AAPL and GOOGL and bought AMZN and NVDA.



Business As Usual ($3,048.65, up $29.09). Holds the S&P 500, and switches into UPRO, a 3x leveraged S&P fund, on days New York weather reads normal for the season on Kalshi's temperature markets. Yes, really. Today was one of those days, so it bought UPRO at $148.44 at the open.



Full Send ($442.36, up 5.30% today). Holds TQQQ, the 3x Nasdaq fund, while the Nasdaq-100 is above its 200 day average, and Treasury bills otherwise. It's the most aggressive thing in the book, and days like today are why it's there.



AI Picks & Shovels ($883.70, up $27.07 today). Owns the AI buildout, chips through networking and power, reweighted by momentum. Today's reweight trimmed SMCI, ANET, DELL and some NVDA, and added AMD, MRVL and TSM.



Pelosi Tracker ($1,896.45, up $27.13, up 1.45%). It mirrors Nancy Pelosi's disclosed stock buys. Today it trimmed AAPL, AMZN and INTC and added Palo Alto Networks at $347.77 off her latest disclosure.



High Profile Congress ($488.57, up $2.85) does the same thing across a group of high volume Congress members. It swapped RARE, RIG, STAG and YETI for FITB, RPM and AT&T off a new filing.



FDA Inspector, down $7.45 today, the worst in the book. It sold its Amgen at $430.93 and bought Pfizer at $29.64. Its first Amgen buy in this run was $377.57.



Dip Buyer is easing new money into VOO only on dip days: about $300 at $704.93 today and a similar amount last Thursday. The rest of its $2,000 is still waiting for the next dip.



NFL Fantasy Agent buys YES on player props for my fantasy roster. It went 1 for 3 Sunday: Blake Corum 40+ rushing yards at 56 cents paid a dollar, while a Browns receiver touchdown and a CeeDee Lamb touchdown both went to zero. Still a lottery ticket and sized like one.

comments.author: Tasty-Mammoth5321
comments.body:
Thanks for the breakdown by sleeve, most posts only show the total. A few things I would want to know before reading too much into it.  
The Kneeler's 89 for 89 sounds strong, but trades inside the same game day are tied together, so it is closer to five observations than 89, and the payoff shape (a small gain per win, a loss that cancels many wins) means a single upset matters a lot. I scored a few thousand resolved Polymarket markets, and the prices on the near certain side were well calibrated, but rules in the style of selling the longshot flipped sign between horizons and between my two halves of the data.  
The weather switch makes me curious. Without a mechanism, if you tried many sleeves and kept the ten that looked best over a couple of weeks, some of them will look good by chance. How many did you try before keeping these? And did you write down a number of weeks or trades you wanted to see before adding the second $10,000, or was it the good stretch itself that decided it?

comments.author: TheObserverDev
comments.body:
i asked cloude to view your post because honestly , i would not understand it if not read very carefully.  and also i built a site so cloude also compares to  my site and determines a marketing strategy,  anyways, here is what cloude said:  Reviewing a mixed-strategy trading app with real money.

Reviewing a mixed-strategy trading app with real money.

That’s someone running **real money** (about $21,000) through an AI-agent trading app. The first screenshot shows an app called “raijin”, with a “Build” tab, so these are strategy bots they set up there. A Robinhood account and two other platforms are connected to it. They’re reporting how each “agent” did that day.

**What the agents are:** a mix of serious ideas and fun experiments:

* **Normal strategies:** momentum in big tech, AI stocks, buying the S&P on dip days.
* **Copycat strategies:** mirroring stock trades that Nancy Pelosi and other Congress members must publicly disclose.
* **Risky ones:** 3x leveraged funds (TQQQ, UPRO), which gain or lose three times what the market does in a day.
* **Betting, not investing:** Kalshi is a prediction market, so “The Kneeler” and “NFL Fantasy Agent” are essentially bets on football games.
* **Quirky ones:** switching to a 3x fund when New York’s weather is “normal for the season”. The poster admits it’s silly, and that’s part of the charm.

**A healthy dose of skepticism:**

* **It’s very short-term.** It’s about a few weeks of results, highlighting one good day (+1.39%). One good day says almost nothing.
* **“89 for 89” sounds amazing but isn’t.** The Kneeler bets 88–99 cents to win $1, small sure-looking wins that a single surprise can wipe out.
* **It may partly be an ad for the app.** That’s common on Reddit. Not necessarily bad, just worth noticing.
* **The numbers are self-reported screenshots.** Nobody can check them.

**Why it’s useful for you:** the post shows why this genre gets attention, and you have the same ingredients plus one advantage:

1. **Bots with names and personalities.** “Pelosi Tracker”, “The Kneeler”, “Full Send” are fun to follow, like your Wine Drinker, Old Man and Claude’s Flywheel.
2. **“What’s working, what isn’t.”** Admitting the worst performer (“FDA Inspector, worst in the book”) makes the post feel honest. Your weekly posts can do the same: “Old Man is down 9.8% and here’s why.”
3. **Specific trades with prices.** “Sold Amgen at $430.93, bought Pfizer at $29.64” is concrete and believable. Your site has exactly that for every bot.
4. **Your edge: proof.** His numbers are screenshots. Yours are **public, locked and checkable by anyone** on bots4stocks.com. Paper money is less exciting than real money, but “you can verify every trade” is something this post can’t offer.         .    well, this is what cloud said, i must add  that cloude and me are learning from you guys,  thank you.    it will help build a better site, post like this helps a lot for my site.
